samples.summary: New clamp makes Decrease at zero destructive when `dp` is stored, breaking the issue's "equal increases and decreases leave the selection exactly as they found it" rule
samples.evidence: The delta replaces `if (target < 0) return;` with `if (dp + delta < 0 && !explicitDp) return;` plus `const target = Math.max(0, dp + delta)`. So when a cell has an explicitly stored `dp: 0` and the value's own precision is also 0 (e.g. `1234` styled `{dp: 0, nf: 'number'}` from the toolbar), pressing Decrease — which the user reads as a no-op at the floor — now takes the `target === valueDp && explicitDp` branch and unsets `{dp, nf}`, dropping the number format and its grouping separators (`1,234` → `1234`). Pressing Increase afterwards does not restore it: it writes `{dp: 1, nf: 'number'}`. One Decrease + one Increase therefore leaves the cell in a different state than it started, which is exactly the reversibility criterion in docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-5 and docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:213-216. Before this delta the same click was an unconditional no-op. It also makes Decrease-at-zero behave differently depending on invisible state (stored vs inferred `dp`), which neither the design doc nor the "Known deviations" list records.

samples.summary: Per-layer value-conflict scan re-implements `hasConflictingStyleSourceForKey` instead of reusing it
samples.evidence: The rewritten loop over sheetStyle/colStyles/rowStyles/rangeStyles at sheet.ts:4257-4286 now performs a value-equality conflict check that is nearly identical in shape to `hasConflictingStyleSourceForKey` in packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/style-mutation.ts:204-252 (same four layers, same `value !== undefined && value !== targetValue` predicate, same `rangesIntersect` patch test). The unset adds an ownership dimension the shared helper lacks, but the duplicated traversal means the two conflict definitions can now drift independently; the repo's reuse expectation would suggest extending the shared helper (e.g. an ownership predicate parameter) rather than a second copy.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: sheet.ts:4197 only short-circuits when `!explicitDp`, sheet.ts:4202 clamps `target` to 0, and sheet.ts:4205-4212 then takes the unset branch whenever `explicitDp && target === valueDp`. For a cell holding `{dp: 0, nf: 'number'}` over an integer (`valueDp = 0`, sheet.ts:4175), a Decrease that the user reads as a floor no-op therefore removes both keys — `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4238-4317) has no guard refusing a single-cell selection whose own `cell.s` matches — dropping the number format and grouping separators, and a following Increase writes `{dp: 1, nf: 'number'}` (sheet.ts:4215-4219), so the pair does not restore the starting state. That conflicts with the headline promise at docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:214-216. Two caveats keep my confidence low rather than making this refutable: (a) the reviewer's assertion that the deviation is unrecorded is wrong — sheet-style.md:233-243 and the todo's Known deviations (80-89) record the nf/separator loss with the same `1,234.5` example and the stored-vs-inferred divergence; (b) strict reversibility at a clamp floor is unattainable in any clamped implementation. But the docs frame the loss as occurring when `dp` is stepped *down to* the value precision, not when it already sits there and the step is clamped, so the flagged case is not squarely covered, and I have no named ground (not-present / already-guarded / clean counterexample) to drop it.

finding.summary: `inheritable` gate narrows the spec'd unset rule, so non-plain/number formats keep residue. The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:50-53) specifies: `target === valueDp` and `explicitDp` → try to unset, using `['dp','nf']` when `nf === 'number'` and **`['dp']` otherwise**. The implementation instead only attempts an unset when `!nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'number'`, so a `currency`/`percent`/date-formatted cell with an explicit `dp` never returns to inheritance: e.g. currency cell holding `12.34` (valueDp 2, default dp 2) → Increase writes `dp: 3` → Decrease targets 2 === valueDp but is blocked by `inheritable`, storing `dp: 2` residue instead of unsetting. That is the same residue class the issue's outcome ("leave a cell exactly as it started") is about, just for a different number format.
finding.evidence: const inheritable = !nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'number'; if (explicitDp && target === valueDp && inheritable) { ... }

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4204-4205, and the `inheritable` gate is not in the spec: the todo (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:55-57) says `target === valueDp` && `explicitDp` → attempt unset with `{dp, nf}` when `nf === 'number'` and `{dp}` *otherwise*, with the outcome (lines 3-5) requiring no `dp`/`nf` left on a cell that had none. The canonical design doc (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:221-225) likewise states the rule with no format restriction, and neither the todo's Known deviations (78-92) nor the doc's Consequences (227-243) records this narrowing. Nothing guards the path: for a currency/percent/date active cell with an explicit `dp`, changeDecimals falls through to `setRangeStyle({dp: target})` (sheet.ts:4215-4219) because line 4216 also skips the `nf` patch for non-plain formats, so `dp` residue is stored (e.g. currency `12.34`: dp default 2 at sheet.ts:4185 → Increase `{dp:3}` → Decrease stores `dp:2`). No test exercises a non-plain active cell; packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:177-205 only covers currency/percent on *other* cells in the selection. This is an unmet acceptance criterion / undocumented deviation, which is major under the design-fit rubric.
